C-3.Name: Add "Copy as HTML": rich text/html clipboard for email paste
C-3.Summary: A native Edit-menu item "Copy as HTML" (id edit.copy-as-html, Cmd+Shift+C) copies the current selection — or the whole document when nothing is selected — to the system clipboard as rich text/html plus Markdown text/plain, so pasting into email clients (Apple Mail, Gmail, Outlook) keeps formatting instead of degrading to raw Markdown.

Problem.Description: Pasting copied content from Mark into email clients loses all formatting. Reason: muya's normal copy (Cmd+C / native predefined Copy) deliberately writes an EMPTY text/html flavor and puts the Markdown source into text/plain (src/muya/lib/contentState/ copyCutCtrl.js copyHandler case 'normal'). Email clients honor text/html first and fall back to text/plain, so the message body ends up with raw Markdown or mangled formatting. The existing muya method copyAsRich produces exactly the needed payload (text/html = rendered HTML regenerated from the selection via marked, text/plain = Markdown), but nothing in the Mark UI exposes it: no menu item, no command id, and its execCommand('copy') transport cannot be triggered from the native menu because WKWebView requires a webview user gesture for execCommand clipboard writes, which a Tauri menu event does not carry.
Problem.Evidence: src/muya/lib/contentState/copyCutCtrl.js copy flavors per _copyType; src/muya/lib/eventHandler/clipboard.js execCommand transport; src/renderer/src/commands/descriptions.js + static/locales/en.json commands.edit.copyAsHtml — palette strings present but no command registered; src-tauri/src/m009_menu.rs Edit submenu had no copy-as item.

Goals.Goal: R-1: Edit-menu item "Copy as HTML" (edit.copy-as-html, Cmd+Shift+C) writes the selection as rich text/html (the same payload muya copyAsRich computes) + Markdown text/plain.
R-2: With no selection, copies the whole document (getMarkdown + muya marked with the editor's muya options) instead of no-op.
R-3: Primary write via native tauri-plugin-clipboard-manager writeHtml (works without webview user gesture); on rejection fall back to muya copyAsRich() execCommand path.
R-4: Command palette discovers the command via existing description key commands.edit.copyAsHtml.
R-6: Menu ↔ command consistency gates stay green and the accelerator is pinned by a source assertion.

GoalAddendum.Description: R-5 as originally written described the pre-review accessor. After review-1 (finding 1: table-cell and image selections fell through to the whole-document copy), getCopyData() returns { text } — the markdown of whatever is selected: DOM ranges delegate to contentState.getClipBoardData().text; selected table cells reuse the docCopyHandler export (1x1 → cell text, multi-cell → createTableInFigure + ExportMarkdown); a selected image returns token.raw. The method is a read-mostly accessor, not a pure query (the range branch may repair the DOM selection or blur the editor when cursor state is invalid — documented in the JSDoc). R-1's "same payload muya copyAsRich computes" applies to DOM ranges; for cells/image the new path produces real rendered HTML (muya's docCopyHandler writes empty text/html there — intentionally better). A single empty selected cell counts as "nothing selected" and falls back to the whole document (R-2).

Constraints.Constraint: No changes to C-2-touched files (ipc/contract/listener.ts, ipc/runtime/watch.ts, store/editor.js, store/project.js, m013b/watch.rs, m_v1_compat.rs) — independent change.
Tauri capability files default.json and mas.json both gain clipboard-manager:allow-write-html (MAS build parity).
muya modification limited to one pure prototype method in src/muya/lib/index.js; vendored muya style preserved.
GRACE anchors updated: graph M-011/M-012 fn entries, verification V-M-009/V-M-011/V-M-012 scenarios/commands, module contracts + CHANGE_SUMMARY in every edited source file.

Release protocol (user mandate, same as C-2): two sequential independent reviews from different angles — review-1 correctness/races/edge-cases, review-2 security/contracts/regressions — must BOTH return clean before the change ships; 100% line+branch coverage required for every changed renderer/muya function; changed Rust code paths pinned by deterministic tests.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Changing normal Cmd+C copy semantics (still Markdown-as-plain-text by muya design).
Exposing muya copyAsHtml (HTML source code as plain text) in the UI; it stays internal.
Inline CSS styling of the copied HTML; the semantic fragment (h1-h6, strong, ul, pre, table) is what email clients style themselves.
Embedding images into the copied HTML; local file paths stay local.
Success toast/notification (silent success, consistent with platform copy UX).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Native Edit menu contains "Copy as HTML" with id edit.copy-as-html and accelerator CmdOrCtrl+Shift+C, and the id resolves to a renderer command.
With a selection, the clipboard text/html flavor holds the rendered HTML fragment and text/plain holds the Markdown (written via clipboard-manager writeHtml).
With no selection over a non-empty document, the whole document is copied (Markdown + muya-marked HTML); with an empty document the command is a no-op.
If the native writeHtml invoke rejects, muya copyAsRich() runs as the execCommand fallback and the failure is logged with the BLOCK_COPY_AS_HTML marker.
All affected vitest suites and cargo menu tests pass; grace lint reports no C-3 issues.

C-3.VerificationIntent: Deterministic unit gates pin every layer: menu-consistency pins the menu id + accelerator against the Rust source and the id ↔ command contract; editor-coverage pins the handler's four paths (selection write, whole-document fallback, empty no-op, native-failure → execCommand fallback) and unmount unregistration; commands index-deep pins the bus emission; muya copy-data pins the pure delegation; cargo m009_menu tests pin Rust menu invariants. The end-user email-paste behavior (mail client prefers text/html) is covered by the R-1 payload contract asserted in editor-coverage.

Approval.ApprovalScope: Copy-as-HTML menu item that puts rich text/html on the clipboard so email paste keeps formatting; whole-document fallback; tests and GRACE evidence.

ReviewLog.Review: MAJOR: table-cell/image selections silently copied the whole document — fixed by extending getCopyData to mirror muya's docCopyHandler/copyHandler special cases. MINOR: null-deref in the catch after mid-flight unmount — fixed with an editor.value re-guard; execCommand fallback is dead from the menu — now supplemented with a user notification (error.copyError). NIT: selection HTML used marked without editor options — fixed by unifying the pipeline (marked(text, options) + DOMPurify on every path). Test gaps (cells-vs-whole-doc, mid-flight unmount, accelerator uniqueness) closed.

Zero CRITICAL/MAJOR. Security: DOMPurify EXPORT config strips script/on*/javascript:/data: — verified; capability grant adds write_html only, no read. Regression: throwaway table export blocks cannot leak into live state (detached objects, same sequence as docCopyHandler). Four MINOR contract gaps fixed: BLOCK_COPY_AS_HTML marker registered in V-M-011; R-5 addendum; V-M-012 scenario-14 + graph fn-getCopyData PURPOSE reworded to the { text } contract; MODULE header added to muya/lib/index.js.
